ctx.x: Yeah, you see, we came to New York with Mamie Smith. She came down -- she was married to a Jewish fella by the name of Bert Goldberg and they came down and got us and we played some theaters and Tim and Freddie -- Timmie Rogers and Freddie was together. We played theaters with her. She was on her -- she was declining, too. She had been a big thing. She was the first blues singer, black blues singer, they had, you know. They called them race records then, you know.

So she brought the whole band to New York. We came to New York with her and we ended up in Buffalo at a place called the Vendome and you know, the bottom started falling out of the band. So when we got back to Cincinnati, it was five bands in the hotel, Delton Syncopaters, Speed Webb -- I

items.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: I worked with Mamie, in later years.

ctx.x: They were singing the Blues, like Mamie Smith, Bessie Smith, Ma Rainey and all of them you know, and they were trying to get away from it. Like what was that other one [sings] If you had plenty money, like 1922, you wouldn’t be here, why don’t you do right like the other folk do, go out and give me some money too. That was made by Ma Rainey, and she was older than Mamie Smith. I worked with Mamie, in later years. And she was older than Mamie Smith. And they didn’t make no money on that. Many did, and Peggy did,…
Any other little anecdotes you’d like to give us?
